item.title: NEW: Capcom Data Breach Exposes Data of Over 11 Million Users
item.description:
Headline: Capcom Data Breach Exposes Data of Over 11 Million Users

Summary:
Japanese gaming company Capcom has confirmed a significant data breach of its CAPCOM ID membership service, impacting over 11.7 million customer accounts. The incident, detected on October 19, 2026, resulted in the unauthorized access and theft of user data including email addresses, IP addresses, and login information. While financial data was not compromised, Capcom is warning all users to be vigilant against phishing attempts. The company has notified authorities and is in the process of contacting affected individuals.

Severity: High

item.title: NEW: eMudhra Intermediate CA Keys Compromised by Cryptographic Flaw
item.description:
Headline: eMudhra Intermediate CA Keys Compromised by Cryptographic Flaw

Summary:
A significant security incident has impacted the public key infrastructure (PKI) following the compromise of eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys from the Indian CA, eMudhra Limited. The compromise stems from a critical cryptographic defect where keys were generated with insufficient randomness, making it possible for attackers to deduce the private keys from public certificates. This flaw enables the creation of fraudulent TLS certificates, posing a severe risk of man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks. Major technology vendors are revoking trust in these CAs, and eMudhra has revoked the affected certificates. Security teams must prioritize updating trust stores and auditing their environments for certificates issued by these compromised CAs.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 6 minutes

Meta Description: Eight intermediate CA private keys from eMudhra were compromised due to insufficient randomness, risking MitM attacks. Browsers and OS vendors are revoking trust.

Article Slug: emudhra-intermediate-ca-certificates-compromised-due-to-cryptographic-flaw

Summary:

Given PHP's ubiquitous use in web servers and content management systems worldwide, the potential impact is massive. Palo Alto Networks' Cortex Xpanse has already identified over 22.6 million exposed instances. A proof-of-concept exploit is known to exist, and at least one European government has taken its website offline as a precaution. Organizations are strongly urged to review the advisory from The PHP Group and apply patches immediately to mitigate the risk of compromise.

item.title: NEW: Actor 'BUGSTER' Uses AI for Credential Theft and VoIP Fraud
item.description:
Headline: Actor 'BUGSTER' Uses AI for Credential Theft and VoIP Fraud

Summary:
A Unit 42 investigation has uncovered a threat actor, tracked as 'BUGSTER', actively weaponizing jailbroken AI tools to plan and execute a range of cybercrimes. The actor utilizes the Hermes Agent framework with the DeepSeek V4 model to bypass safety controls, enabling malicious activities primarily targeting entities in India. Reported operations include conducting a brute-force campaign against a university's WordPress site, successfully exfiltrating a database containing over 5,200 student records from another university, planning VoIP fraud, and running an automated Wi-Fi password cracking pipeline. This case highlights a concerning trend where threat actors are adopting AI to enhance their operational efficiency and sophistication.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Malware, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Analysis

Meta Description: Unit 42 investigation reveals threat actor 'BUGSTER' using AI assistants like DeepSeek to plan and execute cybercrime, including data breaches and VoIP fraud.

item.description:
Headline: ConnectWise Shuts Down Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack

Summary:
IT software provider ConnectWise has suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services following a significant supply-chain attack. The incident involved a compromised application credential for its multitenant OAuth application, which threat actors used to gain unauthorized, high-privilege access to the Microsoft 365 environments of its Managed Service Provider (MSP) partners and their customers. The attack bypassed user-based MFA, leading ConnectWise to take services offline and reset credentials.
